findings.title: Filename collisions retain authorization for overwritten dialogue
findings.body: C4’s session-keyed last-wins map does not reproduce the existing disk reread. Executed the real parser, collector and validator with mocked I/O and the proposed in-memory substitutions: session IDs s_1 and s.1 both write claude-s_1.json. The baseline map contains only the final session, s.1; the proposed map retains both. A false-taint learning counting claude:s_1 is therefore rejected by the baseline but accepted by the proposal, although its scratch dialogue was overwritten by another session. The existing scratch integrity check passes this collision. This introduces an unpriced mismatch between model-visible dialogue and qualifying gate evidence.
findings.recommendation: Specify collision handling that preserves the baseline map’s surviving-file semantics without rereading tool metadata from disk. Add a collector-to-validator test using distinct IDs that sanitize to the same filename.

findings.title: Owner-facing guarantees still contradict the priced deadline residual
findings.body: Owner item 1 still promises an identical admitted set and that F1 cannot worsen. The same unconditional exclusion-set claim survives at spec:349-350 and logbook:61-62. C1a at spec:276 also incorrectly makes one run finishing within the deadline sufficient: the executed counterexample admitted all five projected sessions in 50 ms while the baseline admitted only one under the same 60 ms deadline. Both comparison runs must avoid deadline deferral. These are unresolved round-1 guarantees, not objections to accepting the disclosed residual.
findings.recommendation: Replace the remaining unconditional guarantees with byte-policy equivalence; condition admitted-set equality on both runs avoiding deadline deferral. Apply that qualification to C1a, owner item 1, implementation notes and the logbook.
